question: persister
stimulus:
I will arise and go now, and go to Innisfree,
And a small cabin build there, of clay and wattles made;
Nine bean-rows will I have there, a hive for the honey-bee,
And live alone in the bee-loud glade.

And I shall have some peace there, for peace comes dropping slow,
Dropping from the veils of the morning to where the cricket sings;
There midnight's all a glimmer, and noon a purple glow,
And evening full of the linnet's wings.

I will arise and go now, for always night and day
I hear lake water lapping with low sounds by the shore;
While I stand on the roadway, or on the pavements grey,
I hear it in the deep heart's core.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: "I hear it in the deep heart's core": retrospective capture of pre-primed survivors
ideas.description: Barcode a clonal cancer cell population, split it, treat one half and profile the untreated half by single-cell RNA-seq, then trace survivor barcodes back to their untreated twin cells. This reveals whether the surviving state is a pre-existing transcriptional memory present before drug exposure rather than a drug-induced change.

ideas.title: "Peace comes dropping slow": timescale of transcriptional state fluctuation
ideas.description: Knock in live-cell fluorescent reporters at candidate priming loci (e.g., AXL, NGFR, EGFR) and use long-term timelapse imaging to measure dwell times and autocorrelation of the high-expressing state. Sorting cells by how long they have occupied that state and then challenging them tests whether survival probability depends on the duration, not just the level, of priming.

ideas.title: "In the bee-loud glade": spatial and paracrine determinants of survival
ideas.description: Treat cells at controlled densities and micropatterned spacings, then image survivors in situ with multiplexed single-molecule FISH or spatial transcriptomics to test whether they arise in non-random neighborhoods. Conditioned-medium and transwell co-culture experiments then determine whether tolerance is transferable between neighbors or strictly cell-intrinsic.

ideas.title: "Nine bean-rows and a hive": quiescence and metabolic self-sufficiency of survivors
ideas.description: Combine FUCCI cell-cycle reporters or dye-dilution proliferation tracking with single-cell metabolic readouts such as NAD(P)H FLIM or SCENITH during the first days of treatment. This distinguishes survivors that are simply slow-cycling and metabolically frugal from those running a distinct resistance gene program.

ideas.title: "I will arise and go now" (said twice): reversibility across drug-on/drug-off cycles
ideas.description: Barcode cells and run repeated cycles of treatment and drug holiday, sequencing barcode abundance plus matched single-cell DNA and RNA at each round. Recurrence of the same barcodes indicates heritable genetic or stably epigenetic resistance, whereas a fresh survivor set each cycle indicates a transient, stochastically re-entered state.
